title: A fixed 2.21661-day HARPS wave gives no clear HIRES error reduction for GJ 887
abstract: We test whether the published 2.21661-day candidate of GJ 887 transfers from HARPS to independent HIRES velocities. A fixed wave fitted to 282 HARPS nights has an amplitude of 0.378 m/s. It reduces weighted error in 75 HIRES nights by 1.85 percent. A conditional 30-day block range is -3.08 to +6.45 percent. The test has low power at the reported amplitude and neither confirms nor excludes the candidate. Exact-harmonic, activity, noise and period controls do not give a clear physical cause. A separate reduction audit finds two DRS velocity groups tied to CCF width. Adding group offsets reduces DRS-minus-SERVAL residual RMS from 99.4 to 5.36 m/s. We do not identify the exact reduction cause. The products share spectra. No new planet or signal is found. Code, exact catalog snapshots, hashes, tables, figures and offline instructions are included. Job sci-1107-hp-astronomy-01d5702c9765; machine hp; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: Fixed HARPS waves tested in HIRES. Candidate uncertainty ranges include zero. The block ranges are conditional on the fixed periods and nuisance model.
The public DRS values form two velocity groups tied to CCF width. Separate group offsets reduce residual scatter. The cause is not identified.
